In Los Angeles, Lil Peep initially lived in [Skid Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skid_Row,_Los_Angeles "Skid Row, Los Angeles"), where he dipped in and out of homelessness,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:1-32) staying at Savage's apartment while Savage pursued a degree. The two eventually went separate ways,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:23-27) and Peep met Atlanta rapper and producer JGRXXN, Florida rapper [Ghostemane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghostemane "Ghostemane") and Houston rapper [Craig Xen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Xen "Craig Xen"), living with them while forming the collective Schemaposse.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:4-33) He originally met Craig Xen online and was introduced to JGRXXN, who needed a singer.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-34) Lil Peep also attended [Glendale Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale_Community_College_(California) "Glendale Community College (California)") during his first year in Los Angeles.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:3-21)

In 2015, Peep released his first extended play, _Feelz._ This was followed by his debut mixtape _Lil Peep; Part One_, which generated 4,000 plays in its first week. Shortly thereafter, he released a follow-up mixtape, _[Live Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Forever\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Live Forever (Lil Peep mixtape)")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-36) Feelz was described by Peeps close friends as sounding reminiscent of [Dylan Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Ross "Dylan Ross"), an artist who Lil Peep studied and was inspired by.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-38)

In fall of 2015, Lil Peep began to grow in popularity, garnered by the popularity of songs such as "Star Shopping", later released as a single posthumously,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-39) and made waves in underground hip hop circles.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:4-33) Lil Peep's popularity continued to rise after the release of the song "Beamer Boy", which led to him performing live for the first time with the rest of Schemaposse in February 2016 in [Tucson, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-40) In April, Schemaposse broke up and Lil Peep was no longer associated with a collective, though they remained on good terms.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-41) Shortly after Schemaposse's breakup, Peep began to associate with Los Angeles-based rap collective [GothBoiClique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GothBoiClique "GothBoiClique"), featuring members of the group on his full-length mixtape _[Crybaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crybaby\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Crybaby (Lil Peep mixtape)")_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:3-21) The group shared a squat in Skid Row with Peep and often shared beds.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-The_Guardian-29)_Crybaby_ was recorded over the span of one month and was completed hours before its original release on SoundCloud in June 2016. Peep completed a majority of the mixing and mastering himself.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-HAM_ON_EVERYTHING-24) In August, [First Access Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Access_Entertainment "First Access Entertainment") (FAE) partnered with Lil Peep on a joint venture to invest in and advise him on his career.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-42)

In September 2016, Lil Peep released his fourth and final solo mixtape, _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Hellboy (Lil Peep mixtape)")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-43) Songs from _Hellboy_ such as "Girls" and "OMFG" received millions of views and plays on [SoundCloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoundCloud "SoundCloud") and YouTube.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-44)_Hellboy_'s success led to Peep's first solo tour across the United States and Europe in the spring of 2017, which included performances in Russia and the UK for the first time in his career.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-45) In May 2017, the band [Mineral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineral_(band) "Mineral (band)") accused Peep of [copyright infringement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copyright_infringement "Copyright infringement") for including an unlicensed and uncredited [sample](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_(music) "Sampling (music)") of their song "LoveLetterTypewriter" on his track "Hollywood Dreaming". Peep said that he was only trying to "show some love" with the sample.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-46)

Soon after the tour was completed, Peep was involved in a disentanglement with Gothboiclique, and emigrated to London, England, where he associated with Atlanta rapper iLoveMakonnen and longtime friend Bexey, and recorded _[Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_Over\_When\_You're\_Sober,\_Pt.\_1 "Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1")_ and _[Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_Over\_When\_You're\_Sober,\_Pt.\_2 "Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2")_, the EP [Goth Angel Sinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goth_Angel_Sinner "Goth Angel Sinner") and _Diamonds_ with iLoveMakonnen.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:24-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-49) Peep released his debut studio album, Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1, on August 15, 2017.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:12-50) Shortly thereafter he embarked on his second world tour, beginning in the UK in September[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:25-51) and moving to Germany before finishing in the United States in November, which was cut short by his death.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:26-52)

### Posthumous releases

After his death, Lil Peep's fanbase and popularity grew quickly, resulting in a significant increase in sales and streams of his music.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-53) The single "[Awful Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awful_Things "Awful Things")" from _Come Over When You're Sober, Part One_ charted, becoming his first entry on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 at number 79.

Due to Peep's prolific work rate, a number of songs and projects were completed prior to his death. The first official posthumous release arrived within 24 hours of his death, as Wiggy, a director of many of Peep's music videos, released the official video for the then-unreleased song "16 Lines".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-54) On January 12, 2018, [Marshmello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshmello "Marshmello") officially released a collaboration titled "[Spotlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotlight_(Marshmello_and_Lil_Peep_song) "Spotlight (Marshmello and Lil Peep song)")".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-55) The video for "Spotlight" was released on February 12, 2018. On January 15, 2018, rapper [Juicy J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juicy_J "Juicy J") released the song "Got 'Em Like", which featured Lil Peep and [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-56) On January 27, 2018, SoundCloud rapper Teddy released a song collaboration with Lil Peep, "Dreams & Nightmares".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-57)

In March 2018, Peep's music archive was acquired by [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"). On May 13, 2018, a posthumous single, "[4 Gold Chains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4_Gold_Chains "4 Gold Chains")", featuring [Clams Casino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clams_Casino_(musician) "Clams Casino (musician)"), was released as well as a music video.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-58) A collaboration album between Peep and rapper [iLoveMakonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ILoveMakonnen "ILoveMakonnen") is expected to be released on Makonnen's label Warner Bros.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-59) On August 17, 2018, Makonnen announced a new Lil Peep single, "[Falling Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falling_Down_(Lil_Peep_and_XXXTentacion_song) "Falling Down (Lil Peep and XXXTentacion song)")", a reworking of "Sunlight on Your Skin" that he recorded with Peep in the fall of 2017 in London. The new version features recently deceased rapper [XXXTentacion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXXTentacion "XXXTentacion"), who recorded his verses following Peep's death.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-60) The creation of the single was condemned by some surviving members of GothBoiClique, who said there had been unresolved conflict between the two artists stemming from latter's alleged [history of violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XXXTentacion#Legal_issues "XXXTentacion") towards women.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Daramola-61) This was disputed by other close friends of Lil Peep.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-hotnewhiphop.com-62) "Falling Down" was released on September 19, 2018, and peaked at number 13 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-fallingdown-63) The original "Sunlight on Your Skin" was released on September 27, 2018.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-64)

On October 14, 2018, Lil Peep's estate revealed that his first posthumous project, _Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2_, was finished in September 2018 and Lil Peep's executive producer for the project, Smokeasac, confirmed that it was just awaiting approval from Peep's family.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-65) On October 17, 2018, Lil Peep's estate confirmed that the lead single from _Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2,_ "Cry Alone", would be released on October 18, 2018.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-66)_Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2_ was released on November 9, 2018.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:16222-67) On November 1, 2018, the second single from the album, "[Runaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_(Lil_Peep_song) "Runaway (Lil Peep song)")", was officially released.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-68) On November 7, 2018, the third single, "[Life is Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_Is_Beautiful_(Lil_Peep_song) "Life Is Beautiful (Lil Peep song)")"—a remix of the track "Life" from the _Feelz_ EP—was released.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-69)

_Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2_ debuted at number four on the _Billboard_ 200 with 81,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") (including 43,000 pure album sales), making it Lil Peep's first US top 10 album.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-BB2002-10)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-70)

On January 31, 2019, the first single from the upcoming collaboration album with iLoveMakonnen, "[I've Been Waiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've_Been_Waiting "I've Been Waiting")", featuring [Fall Out Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_Out_Boy "Fall Out Boy"), was released.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-71) The song was originally a demo by ILoveMakonnen; Peep then performed on it, spawning a partnership that created up to 20 songs. Fall Out Boy was added to the song after Peep's death.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-72)

On March 10, 2019, the documentary _[Everybody's Everything](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody's\_Everything\_(film) "Everybody's Everything (film)")_, which chronicles Lil Peep's life, premiered at the [SXSW Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SXSW_Film_Festival "SXSW Film Festival").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-73) On November 1, 2019, the estate announced the release of the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody's_Everything_(album) "Everybody's Everything (album)") to the documentary, which features both previously released and unreleased tracks.

In April 2019, "Gym Class" and "Star Shopping", two Lil Peep singles that were originally released in March 2016 and August 2015 respectively, were re-released onto all streaming platforms by the Lil Peep estate.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-74) The 2016 EP _Vertigo_ was subsequently released by the estate to streaming platforms on March 5, 2020.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-75) The Peep estate officially released the _Crybaby_ mixtape with most samples cleared to all streaming platforms on June 10, 2020, to coincide with the four-year anniversary of the original release.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:11-76) The track "falling 4 me" was missing as it could not be cleared with Radiohead.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:11-76) The estate released the _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Hellboy (Lil Peep mixtape)")_ mixtape with most samples cleared on September 25, 2020, the fourth anniversary of its original release.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-77) The song "drive by" was reproduced due to sample clearance issues.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-78)

On January 26, 2021, the estate announced that the _California Girls_ EP was to be re-released.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-79) It was released on January 29, 2021, with a music video for the song "lil kennedy".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-80) Later, on June 30, 2021, the estate announced the re-release of the Lil Peep and Lil Tracy collaboration EPs, _Castles_ and _Castles II_. They were released on July 2, 2021, with video of past live performances of certain tracks from the EPs. In the fall of 2021, the estate released _Friends_ and _High Fashion_, two previously unreleased EPs made in collaboration with Yunggoth and [Harry Fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Fraud "Harry Fraud"), respectively.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-81) On May 20, 2022, the _Feelz_ EP was re-released, with the videos for "feelz" and "life" also being released.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-EDMDemons.com_2022-82) On December 2, 2022, the mixtape _[Live Forever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Forever\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Live Forever (Lil Peep mixtape)")_ was re-released, with the music video for the mixtape's title track also being released.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Twitter-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-84)

On September 1, 2023, the estate released the collaboration with [ILoveMakonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ILoveMakonnen "ILoveMakonnen") "November" on all platforms. The estate also confirmed the duo's 2017 collaboration album _Diamonds_ would be released on September 8, 2023.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-85)

On November 10, 2023, the estate released the project _Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2 (OG Version)_.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-86) The album features the original recorded versions of nine songs from the eventual _Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2_ release from 2018. It also featured the first official release of the song "in the car".

In March 2024, the estate released _Hate Me_, the previously unreleased EP that included the original version of "Spotlight".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-87)_Teen Romance_, a collaborative EP with Lederrick, was re-released in June 2024.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-88)

His debut mixtape, _Lil Peep; Part One_, was re-released on September 18, 2024, to coincide with the nine-year anniversary of its original release.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-89) On November 1, 2024, which would have been Lil Peep's 28th birthday, the estate released the song "Latitude".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-90) The track was originally recorded in 2014, and was one of the first songs he ever made.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-91)

## Fashion

Lil Peep had been interested in fashion since his teenage years, and during the last months of his life he modelled for [Vlone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlone_(brand) "Vlone (brand)") and was invited to and attended several fashion shows such as [Balmain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balmain_(fashion_house) "Balmain (fashion house)") men's show at [Paris Fashion Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Fashion_Week "Paris Fashion Week") and [Moncler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moncler "Moncler") Gamme Bleu MFW Mens Spring Summer show in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Fashion_Week "Milan Fashion Week").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:14222-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:15-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-94) Nico Amarca of _Hypebeast_ said, "Even though Peep's brand of trendy sits on a far more niche spectrum than most modern-day tastemakers, something that largely attributed to his success. In a time where genuine individuality is becoming increasingly obsolete, Peep was the tattoo-covered, Manic Panic-hued mall rat the creative world needed to disrupt its ever-growing homogeny."[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-HYPEBEAST-95) Rapper [Playboi Carti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playboi_Carti "Playboi Carti") described Lil Peep as a "trendsetter".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-HYPEBEAST-95)

His style has been described as evoking fashion styles associated with emo[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-96) and [mall goth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mall_goth "Mall goth").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Vogue_Death-97) He often wore items including graffitied jackets, colored fur,[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-98) and pink clothes.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Vogue_Death-97) He cited [Fat Mike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat_Mike "Fat Mike"), Marcelo Burlon and [the Casualties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Casualties "The Casualties") as style influences. In a 2017 interview with _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_, he stated:

> I never dress the same way for a week—I'll dress like a whole other person the next week. I like to get weird and mix things. Not necessarily draw on the streets, but mix darker, dirtier cultures with high class shit. And kind of fuse them together and see how they can become one. And I think that already happens when I put on any really elegant piece of clothing, because of the way I look. You expect me to dress like a fucking punk.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:14222-92)

In late 2018, it was announced that a Lil Peep clothing line was being created called "No Smoking" (stylized as "NO SMOK!NG") which was developed before Lil Peep's death.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-99)

Lil Peep was described as making [lo-fi rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo-fi_music "Lo-fi music"),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-103) being an "emo-trap heart throb"[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tiny_Mix_Tapes-104) and an "emo rapper".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-AllMusic-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Nme-106) Music journalists often compared Lil Peep to singer-songwriter and guitarist [Kurt Cobain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Cobain "Kurt Cobain").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Robles-107)_[New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_York\_Times "New York Times")_ music critic [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") defined Peep as the [Kurt Cobain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Cobain "Kurt Cobain") of lo-fi rap, describing his music as gloomy and diabolically melodic.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-108) Lil Peep himself encouraged the connection and persona in his musical and lyrical content, saying that he wanted to become the "New Kurt Cobain".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Robles-107)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:0-15) According to Angus Harrison from _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_, Lil Peep was "repurposing Kurt Cobain for bedroom diarists who are more used to rap than they are guitars."[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Harrison-109)

[AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") described Lil Peep's music as a blend of [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop") and rock influences along with [trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_music_(hip_hop) "Trap music (hip hop)"), [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock"), and [dream pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream_pop "Dream pop").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:5-110) His songs generally drew on the [triple-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triple_metre "Triple metre")[hi-hats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hats "Hi-hats") of [Southern rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_rap "Southern rap") and the angsty introspection of [post-hardcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-hardcore "Post-hardcore").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Harrison-109) He combined elements of emo and [pop-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-punk "Pop-punk") into rap music, bringing a fresh take on the genre.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) This resulted in him being described as the "future of emo" by Steven J. Horowitz of online magazine _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6)

Lil Peep is recognised for [sampling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sampling_(music) "Sampling (music)") beginning from his early career,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-111) including material of rock bands such as [Blink-182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink-182 "Blink-182"), [Real Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Friends_(band) "Real Friends (band)"), [Underoath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underoath "Underoath"), [Death Cab for Cutie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_Cab_for_Cutie "Death Cab for Cutie"), [Brand New](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_New_(band) "Brand New (band)"),[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-112)[Red Hot Chili Peppers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hot_Chili_Peppers "Red Hot Chili Peppers"), [Oasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oasis_(band) "Oasis (band)"), [Avenged Sevenfold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avenged_Sevenfold "Avenged Sevenfold"), [Thirty Seconds to Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty_Seconds_to_Mars "Thirty Seconds to Mars"), [The Cure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cure "The Cure"), [Marilyn Manson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Manson_(band) "Marilyn Manson (band)") and [Evanescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evanescence "Evanescence"),[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-113) among others.

As a burgeoning artist, Lil Peep gained a significant amount of traction in the [alternative hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_hip-hop "Alternative hip-hop") scene, establishing a better platform for himself to speak to fans about topics of his concern such as [mental health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_health "Mental health").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Bell-3) His lyrical themes include topics such as [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_disorder "Mood disorder"), [drug use](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_abuse "Substance abuse"), past relationships, and [suicidal thoughts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicidal_thoughts "Suicidal thoughts") and meshes together third-wave emo, alternative rock, pop-punk and dream pop with trap music and hip-hop.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:5-110) A close friend and the executive producer of _Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1_ said that Peep "wanted to give a voice to people that suffer from anxiety and depression, people who have been abused, bullied, and the people who were misunderstood like him. He had demons of his own and he faced those demons by creating music."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-For_Lil_Peep-25)

## Personal life

Lil Peep was candid about struggles with his sexuality, depression, heartbreak, and drug use.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Brandle-114) Lil Peep came out as [bisexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisexual "Bisexual") in a Twitter post on August 8, 2017.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-116)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) He took to Twitter to open up about this aspect of his personal life to his fans.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Bell-3) Lil Peep simply stated, "yes i'm bi sexual."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) After coming out as bisexual, he would regularly confront [homophobes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homophobes "Homophobes") on Twitter.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Greene-117) He was also known collaborators with [iLoveMakonnen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ILoveMakonnen "ILoveMakonnen"), an openly gay recording artist whose music also blurs the line between rap and rock.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Greene-117)

Lil Peep came out around the time he and actress and singer [Bella Thorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bella_Thorne "Bella Thorne") began dating in September 2017.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-118) Shortly after the release of his debut studio album, the two were spotted kissing. They briefly dated, before Thorne became involved with rapper [Mod Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_Sun "Mod Sun").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) While on the [Come Over When You're Sober tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come_Over_When_You're_Sober,_Pt._1 "Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1"), Lil Peep had met and started dating Instagram influencer Arzaylea Rodriguez around the time of his death in November.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Peisner_Peisner_2019-119)

Lil Peep actively talked about his issues with depression, [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety "Anxiety") and [substance abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_abuse "Substance abuse") and stated that he had [bipolar disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipolar_disorder "Bipolar disorder").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:13-4) Alongside drug use, Lil Peep struggled with [suicidal impulses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicidal_ideation "Suicidal ideation") that date back to his adolescent years.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Blend-120) On the track "OMFG" from his breakthrough mixtape _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Hellboy (Lil Peep mixtape)")_, Lil Peep talked about wanting to kill himself.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121) During an interview, he was asked if he was suicidal. Lil Peep replied, "Yeah, it is serious. I suffer from depression and some days I wake up and I'm like, Fuck, I wish I didn't wake up. That was part of why I moved to California, trying to get away from the place that was doing that to me, and the people I was around."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121) He continued, "I realized it was just myself—it's a [chemical imbalance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_imbalance "Chemical imbalance") in my brain. Some days I'll be very down and out, but you won't be able to tell, really, because I don't express that side of myself on social media. That's the side of myself that I express through music. That's my channel for letting all that shit out."[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121) He claims the frankness with which he spoke about difficulties in his life led to an intense connection with his fans through his music. In an interview with _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times "The Times")_, Lil Peep stated, "They tell me that it saved their lives. They say that I stopped them from committing suicide, which is a beautiful thing. ... It's great for me to hear. It helps. It boosts me, because music saved my life as well."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Blend-120)

Lil Peep was not medicated for depression. While those around him insisted, he did not want to, and opted to instead [smoke cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)") and consume whichever other drugs came his way.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121) In his final interview before his death, Peep confessed that his depression was getting worse, saying: "Things just get worse. Things already get worse and worse and worse every day."[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-122) Lil Peep regularly referenced [addictions to cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine_addiction "Cocaine addiction"), [ecstasy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MDMA "MDMA") and [Xanax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xanax "Xanax") in his lyrics and posts on social media.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-123)

At the time of his death, Lil Peep was residing in [Portobello Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portobello_Road "Portobello Road"), London, with his friend and close collaborator Bexey,[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-124)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:13-4) and Smokeasac. The move was provoked by Peep's need to escape his circumstances and his then-collective GothBoiClique.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:24-48)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-pitchfork-102)

## Death

On November 15, 2017, Lil Peep was found dead on his tour bus when his manager went to check on him in preparation for that night's performance at a [Tucson, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tucson,_Arizona "Tucson, Arizona"), venue.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-125) Foul play was not suspected,[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-auto-126) with his death believed to be from an overdose.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-127) In a series of [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") posts in the hours leading up to his death, Lil Peep claimed to have ingested [psilocybin mushrooms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psilocybin_mushrooms "Psilocybin mushrooms") and [cannabis concentrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_concentrate "Cannabis concentrate"). In another post, he claimed to have consumed six [alprazolam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alprazolam "Alprazolam") pills following a video depicting his attempts to drop an unidentified pill into his mouth several times before successfully swallowing one and shaking a full prescription bottle. A subsequent post was captioned, "When I die, you'll love me."[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-128) In the days after his death, a police report revealed that Lil Peep had taken a nap around 5:45 p.m. before the concert. His manager checked on him twice and found him sleeping and breathing fine, but was unable to wake him. When the manager checked on Lil Peep a third time, he was unresponsive and not breathing. Lil Peep's manager performed [CPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPR "CPR") before medics arrived, though he was pronounced dead at the scene.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-129)

On December 8, [Pima County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pima_County "Pima County")'s Office of the Medical Examiner certified his cause of death as an accidental overdose from the powerful pain medication [fentanyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fentanyl "Fentanyl") and the [benzodiazepine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzodiazepine "Benzodiazepine")[alprazolam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alprazolam "Alprazolam"), a [sedative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sedative "Sedative").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-deathofficial-11) Toxicology tests were also positive for [THC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/THC "THC"), [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"), and the [opioid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opioid "Opioid") painkiller [tramadol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tramadol "Tramadol"). Urine tests also showed the presence of multiple powerful opioids, including [hydrocodone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrocodone "Hydrocodone"), [hydromorphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydromorphone "Hydromorphone"), [oxycodone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxycodone "Oxycodone") and [oxymorphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxymorphone "Oxymorphone"). There was no alcohol in his system.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-people-1)

### Wrongful death lawsuit

The rapper's mother Liza Womack filed a [wrongful death claim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrongful_death_claim#United_States "Wrongful death claim") against Lil Peep's management [FAE grp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAE_grp "FAE grp") in 2019, accusing them of "negligence and other breaches of contract which, the lawsuit alleges, contributed to his death in 2017 of an accidental drug overdose." Among the claims in the lawsuit are that FAE was complicit in providing access to "illegal drugs" and "prescription medications", and that the company knowingly allowed drug use to take place during the rapper's tour "despite being aware of his addiction". At one point, the lawsuit charges that FAE encouraged the star to take drugs.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-CMU_2019-130) In a responding statement, FAE expressed disappointment in the lawsuit:

> Lil Peep's death from an accidental drug overdose was a terrible tragedy. However, the claim that First Access Entertainment, any of its employees, or Chase Ortega, or anyone else under our auspices, was somehow responsible for, complicit in, or contributed to his death is categorically untrue. In fact, we consistently encouraged Peep to stop abusing drugs and to distance himself from the negative influence of the drug users and enablers with whom he chose to associate.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-CMU_2019-130)

FAE formally filed court documents at the [Los Angeles County Superior Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Superior_Court "Los Angeles County Superior Court") on December 23, 2019, to dispute all claims, including claims of negligence, breach of contract, "and wrongful death". Stennett told _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ that "[she] felt very protective of Lil Peep from day one." In later documents and court filings, the company said that their work with Lil Peep was an "arm's length business arrangement", something disputed by the rapper's mother.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-131)

Despite court filings, FAE supported the release of Peep's first [posthumous](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/posthumous "wikt:posthumous") album _[Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_Over\_When\_You're\_Sober,\_Pt.\_2 "Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 2")_ (2018), which reached number four on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart, a career-best for the rapper.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-132) At the start of 2020, the company released statements about their belief that they had no contractual responsibility for Lil Peep's personal life, and that a ruling to suggest so would damage management businesses, "Imposing a duty on FAE Ltd. or FAE LLC to prevent [Lil Peep's] drug overdose would extend the boundaries of legal obligations far beyond any precedent, and far beyond the contractual obligations and reasonable expectations of parties doing business. It would convert businesses engaged in the music and entertainment industries into full-time babysitters for artists. That clearly was not the parties' intent upon entering 'the JVA [(joint-venture agreement)].'"[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-MBW_JVAs-133)

After four years in the court system, the lawsuit was settled in February 2023 before going to trial.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-134) While the majority of the terms of the settlement were not made public, it was revealed that, moving forward, Peep's entire catalog of music would move from FAE to the care of his surviving family.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-135)

## Legacy and influence

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/LilPeep-Hellboy_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-LilPeep-Hellboy_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LilPeep-Hellboy_(cropped).jpg)

Before his death, Lil Peep was believed to be on track in taking [SoundCloud rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoundCloud_rap "SoundCloud rap") into the pop mainstream.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-End-150)

Before dying at the age of 21, Lil Peep came to be an inspiration to outcasts and [youth subcultures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Youth_subculture "Youth subculture") drawn together by the internet.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Hypebeast-151) He earned legions of fans in a short time from both [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop") and [emo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emo_Subculture "Emo Subculture") subcultures.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Kornhaber-152) Although he did not claim so himself, he is widely considered to have made a style of music that has been since regarded "emo rap".[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Eloise-153)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Harrison-109) He has been credited as the leading figure of the mid–late 2010s [emo music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emo_music "Emo music") scene[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-154) and is commonly cited as an inspiration for upcoming emo rappers.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-155)

> At the time of Lil Peep's death, he was on the cusp of something significant. Three months earlier, he'd released _[Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Come\_Over\_When\_You're\_Sober,\_Pt.\_1 "Come Over When You're Sober, Pt. 1")_, the album that took the skeleton sound he'd developed in his bedroom – emo sentimentality, thunderous hip-hop underbelly, rock-star insouciance – and thickened it up. His mixtapes _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(Lil\_Peep\_mixtape) "Hellboy (Lil Peep mixtape)")_ and _Crybaby_, released on SoundCloud, were on the front lines of hip-hop's open-eared engagement with other genres, as well as documents of the ways emo and pop-punk had begun to make room for hip-hop. He was at the musical vanguard and, covered in a symphony of tattoos, an emerging fashion icon as well. – _New York Times_ music critic [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica")[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:24-48)

In 2017, _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ hailed Lil Peep as "the future of emo".[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) Regarding his death, in January 2018, [John Jeremiah Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jeremiah_Sullivan "John Jeremiah Sullivan") of _[GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")_ wrote, "When Lil Peep died late last year, he left behind an outsized legacy."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-156)_[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ journalist Elias Leight concurred similarly and wrote that Lil Peep's "rise to stardom was powered by relentless drive."[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-beachside-148) A profile on his artistry was written by _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_ editor Steven Horowitz.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) The lengthy article resulted in an influx of [think pieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Think_piece "Think piece") centered around Lil Peep among writers, with music publications such as _[Noisey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noisey "Noisey")_ discussing his role within the broader emo genre. Though it allowed Peep to gather attention from a wide audience beyond his SoundCloud base, the piece polarized readers, some of whom protested applying the "future of emo" label to the young rapper in the headline.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Eloise-153)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Tenreyro-6) However, Lil Peep has since become regarded being an integral part of a "[post-emo revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-emo_revival "Post-emo revival") style of [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop "Hip hop") and rock",[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:17-157)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garland-158)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Greene-117) and had been described as "arguably the biggest emo icon of the past few years"[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-:21-159)

The death of Lil Peep left an impact on several of his musical contemporaries.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Valentine-160)[Lil Uzi Vert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Uzi_Vert "Lil Uzi Vert") offered tribute by sharing on Twitter an edited version of one of the final photos Lil Peep had shared online.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Valentine-160) The news of Lil Peep's death greatly affected Lil Uzi Vert, who shortly tweeted, "We would love 2 stop ..... but do you really care cause we been on [xanax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xanax "Xanax") all fucking year. [...] Rip buddy I 100% understand and I don't fault u."[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Valentine-160) The prescription pills [Xanax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xanax "Xanax") has since become an epidemic in the hip hop realm, particularly among the current SoundCloud generation.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Newstead-161) The [SoundCloud rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoundCloud_rap "SoundCloud rap") scene Lil Peep originated from is notorious for its drug use, with artists often abusing prescription pills such as Xanax which have since become a go-to [metaphor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphor "Metaphor") in their lyrics.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Brown,_August-162) In an assessment of the reactions, many were hopeful Lil Peep's death has served as a wake-up call for the community regarding [drug abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_abuse "Drug abuse").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Newstead-161) After offering their thoughts, Lil Uzi Vert indicated they were looking to do something for themselves in response to Lil Peep's untimely death.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Newstead-161) Lil Uzi Vert also seemed to make attempts to [detox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detox "Detox"), and the following Thursday tweeted an update saying they were [sober](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobriety "Sobriety") for the day and already shaking.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Valentine-160)

In the years following his death, Lil Peep became influential on the development of the [e-girls and e-boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-girls_and_e-boys "E-girls and e-boys") subculture.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-163) In addition to calling him "the future of emo", _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork\_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ also posited that Lil Peep's willingness to be vulnerable was an antidote to the toxic attitude towards women, which in the past has been a core element of hip-hop culture and its [rap-rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap-rock "Rap-rock") variant.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Weiss-2) Following his death, _[Mic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mic\_(media\_company) "Mic (media company)")_ bemoaned: "Sadly, Peep had barely just begun bringing emo into the future with a message that many of his less woman-friendly influences, like [Brand New](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_New_(band) "Brand New (band)"), have failed to put forward." He continued saying, "For a 'crybaby' who left this world so young, Peep inspired a lot of people to keep going."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Weiss-2) The day after hearing news of his death, rapper [Lil B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_B "Lil B") paid tribute on Twitter, writing: "I remember Lil peep telling me he is against the [sexual abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_abuse "Sexual abuse") of women and people in the music industry... I will continue to push his vision."[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-164)

### Achievements

Having arisen from the SoundCloud scene, Lil Peep had a large presence on social media and came to be revered online.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garland-158)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Harrison-109) He attracted a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following") through the songs he released and their emotional, downtrodden lyrics.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-The_Associated_Press-165) Lil Peep also enjoyed the draw of his YouTube channel, where several millions of views were generated by his music videos for "Awful Things", "[Benz Truck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benz_Truck "Benz Truck")", "[The Brightside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brightside "The Brightside")" among others.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Brandle-114)

According to _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_, "If you were going to bet on the young musicians most likely to soon be superstars, until yesterday, a lot of smart money would have been on Lil Peep."[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Kornhaber-152) Lil Peep had a promising career since 2015 due to a series of tracks, [EPs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EPs "EPs") and [mixtapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixtape "Mixtape") released on SoundCloud.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Brandle-114) After being around for a little more than a year, Lil Peep had already managed to amass millions of hits on YouTube and SoundCloud.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garland-158) A year after posting his first song, Lil Peep attracted 82,000 followers on SoundCloud and 112,000 followers on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Horowitz-121) The burgeoning rapper had generated millions of online [streams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") before releasing his debut album _Come Over When You're Sober Pt. 1_ in August 2017.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garrett-166) Despite being involved with [GothBoiClique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GothBoiClique "GothBoiClique") for the shortest amount of time, Lil Peep became the first member of the group to be paid serious critical attention as well as tour internationally.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garland-158) Due in part to his divisive nature, Lil Peep made his way onto _Pitchfork_'s "Best Songs of the Year" list and completed a largely sold-out tour of Russia and Europe.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Peep#cite_note-Garland-158)

Extraction uses the original question and current page, not the search query or

During navigation, a supplied local relation is a task, not evidence. Follow links
that establish or contradict it. Return when it is settled or has no useful route
here; other unresolved relations belong to the parent. Do not solve the whole
question again inside every branch.

Preserve exact relevant names and rows with their headers, values, units, dates
and scope. Never replace relevant rows with ellipses, examples or instructions to
continue the list. If all rows cannot fit, prioritize rows useful to the question
and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

Follow links likely to fill a candidate's missing condition or reach the required
document/year. An index is useful when it offers a concrete route to the needed
record; generic menus or keyword collections alone do not justify expansion.
Link-menu rank is only a hint: check the destination's subject and scope. If content
repeats, try a detail page or another supported route. Links outside the menu and inferred
paths on an observed site are allowed. Child notes are returned automatically;
do not copy their facts into your own note. Retain useful unvisited links even
when expansion stops.

**Evidence:** Exact relevant facts/rows and short supporting quotes.

**Expand:** yes or no, and why.

incomplete evidence, or not_found with a brief reason. During navigation, call

## About

5,316,476 monthly listeners

A visionary artist who effortlessly blends avant-garde and pop elements, Björk makes music that is as innovative as it is emotional. When the Icelandic singer, songwriter, producer, composer, and multi-instrumentalist launched her solo career, she traded the arty guitar rock of her former group [the Sugarcubes](spotify:artist:1G0Xwj8mza6b03iYkVdzDP) for dance music and worked with some of the genre's biggest names, including [Nellee Hooper](spotify:artist:1l7aiSjBGkQiyTuQYTigAP), [Underworld](spotify:artist:1PXHzxRDiLnjqNrRn2Xbsa), and [Tricky](spotify:artist:6hhA8TKRNryM8FNzqCqdDO). She established her new artistic direction with 1993's Debut, an international, multi-platinum hit that she followed with two equally groundbreaking albums: 1995's Post, another wildly successful work that reflected her style at its poppiest even as it fused jazz, industrial, and different flavors of electronic music, and 1997's Homogenic, an uncompromising fusion of strings and fractured beats that foreshadowed her increasingly experimental direction in the years to come. She swung from the daring softness of 2001's Vespertine to the primal vocal textures of 2004's Medúlla, and found new ways to connect humanity, technology, and music on 2011's Biophilia. Later in the 2010s and into the next decade, Björk delivered powerful expressions of loss and renewal with albums including 2015's Vulnicura and 2022's Fossora, both of which reaffirmed her as one of the most influential and distinctively creative talents of her times. Born in Reykjavik in 1965 to activist Hildur Rúna Hauksdóttir, Björk spent her early years living in a commune with her mother and stepfather Sævar Árnason, who was a guitarist in the band Pops. She studied piano and flute at the Reykjavik school Barnamúsíkskóli; when she sang [Tina Charles](spotify:artist:7Jbs4wPCLaKXPxrTxZ2zaa)' "I Love to Love" at a recital, her teachers sent a recording to Iceland's Radio One that was then broadcast across the nation. A contract with the Fálkinn record label followed, and Björk recorded her self-titled debut album when she was 11. Released in Iceland in December 1977, Björk became a hit within Iceland and contained covers of several pop songs, including [the Beatles](spotify:artist:3WrFJ7ztbogyGnTHbHJFl2)' "Fool on the Hill." As the '70s came to a close, the punk revolution changed Björk's musical tastes. She formed the post-punk group [Exodus](spotify:artist:76S65NHJHrNy4JTrXHP2BH) in 1979 and sang in Jam 80 the following year. In 1981, Björk and [Exodus](spotify:artist:76S65NHJHrNy4JTrXHP2BH) bassist [Jakob Magnusson](spotify:artist:7pQYUlV0pHGolqqTepsuxu) formed Tappi Tikarrass, which released an EP, Bitid Fast I Vitid, on [Spor](spotify:search:label%3A%22Spor%22) later that year; it was followed by the full-length Miranda in 1983. Following Tappi Tikarrass, she formed the goth-tinged post-punk group [KUKL](spotify:artist:1Kuzl5TprdfmyLnBlZiYVn) with Einar Orn Benediktsson. [KUKL](spotify:artist:1Kuzl5TprdfmyLnBlZiYVn) released two albums, The Eye (1984) and Holidays in Europe (1986), on [Crass Records](spotify:search:label%3A%22Crass+Records%22). During this time, Björk published a book of poetry, 1984's Um Úrnat frá Björk and appeared in her first film, The Juniper Tree (which was released in 1990). When Kukl dissolved in mid-1986, Björk, Benediktsson, and other former members founded the [Smekkleysa](spotify:search:label%3A%22Smekkleysa%22) ("Bad Taste") arts collective, which included [the Sugarcubes](spotify:artist:1G0Xwj8mza6b03iYkVdzDP) among its projects. [The Sugarcubes](spotify:artist:1G0Xwj8mza6b03iYkVdzDP) quickly became stars within their homeland and were also one of the rare Icelandic bands to achieve international success when their debut album, Life's Too Good, became a British and American hit in 1988. While the band was on hiatus following the Here Today, Tomorrow Next Week! tour, Björk pursued other projects, including Gling-Gló, a 1990 set of jazz standards and originals with an Icelandic bebop group called Trio Gudmundar Ingolfssonar, and a collaboration with [Current 93](spotify:artist:7vF3DcPluq6lZI36VniagW). She also wrote her own songs and appeared on two songs on [808 State](spotify:artist:7hFdUW64G4iU1tz46ITRfN)'s 1991 album ex:el, an experience that sparked her love of house music. After recording and touring in support of [the Sugarcubes](spotify:artist:1G0Xwj8mza6b03iYkVdzDP)' final album, 1992's Stick Around for Joy, Björk moved to London and embarked on her solo career. Working with [Massive Attack](spotify:artist:6FXMGgJwohJLUSr5nVlf9X)'s [Nellee Hooper](spotify:artist:1l7aiSjBGkQiyTuQYTigAP) as her co-producer, she combined new compositions with songs she had written as a teenager and drew from influences such as Bollywood, exotica, and jazz as well as electronic music. Featuring contributions from [Talvin Singh](spotify:artist:30Y7JOpiNgAGEhnkYPdI1P), jazz harpist [Corky Hale](spotify:artist:7B20tHBVKVg3b6K3W1OKwo) and reedist [Oliver Lake](spotify:artist:3y58dknRdBENZ8oVErWu9B), Debut -- so named by Björk to underscore its musical fresh start -- appeared in June 1993. It quickly became her most successful project to date: the album earned widespread critical acclaim and reached number two on the charts in Iceland and number three on the U.K. Album Charts. Debut went double platinum in the U.K. and platinum in four other countries, including the U.S., and was certified gold in five other countries. Boosted by an eye-catching Michel Gondry video, the single "Human Behaviour" became a Top 40 hit in the U.K., followed by "Venus as a Boy," "Big Time Sensuality," and "Violently Happy." At the end of the year, NME magazine named Debut the album of the year, while she won International Female Solo Artist and Newcomer at the BRIT Awards; at the 1994 Grammy Awards, Gondry's video was nominated for Best Short Form Music Video. Björk followed Debut's success with a number of collaborations. "Play Dead," a collaboration with [David Arnold](spotify:artist:6xpxzGS2J2tijVVWp2RY0j) recorded for the film The Young Americans, appeared shortly after the album's release and was included as a bonus track on a rerelease. In 1994, she lent her vocals to [Plaid](spotify:artist:5akVqMzdZOdbMYbE4vNZWD)'s album Not for Threes, co-wrote [Madonna](spotify:artist:6tbjWDEIzxoDsBA1FuhfPW)'s "Bedtime Stories," and appeared in an uncredited role in Robert Altman's film Prêt-à-Porter. She also worked on her second album with [Hooper](spotify:artist:1l7aiSjBGkQiyTuQYTigAP), [Tricky](spotify:artist:6hhA8TKRNryM8FNzqCqdDO), [808 State](spotify:artist:7hFdUW64G4iU1tz46ITRfN)'s Graham Massey, and [Howie B](spotify:artist:1DAJPl1Q9bNwPGUqL08nzG) of [Mo' Wax Records](spotify:search:label%3A%22Mo%27+Wax+Records%22); as her co-producers; her other collaborators included [Talvin Singh](spotify:artist:30Y7JOpiNgAGEhnkYPdI1P) and Brazilian composer and conductor [Eumir Deodato](spotify:artist:0hE3uA2w3guHeKvuc7BpRr). Recorded in Nassau and London, June 1995's Post further broadened Björk's musical horizons, incorporating industrial, ambient, IDM, trip-hop, and jazz into its bustling portrait of her life after moving to London. Hailed for its fusion of pop and experimental music, the album was another critical success as well as on the charts. Post was a Top Ten hit in over 20 countries (including the U.K., where it reached number two) and peaked at number 32 in the U.S. It was certified platinum in four countries, including the U.K. and the U.S., and was certified gold in four more. Post yielded the singles "Army of Me," "Isobel," "Hyperballad" and "It's Oh So Quiet," the latter of which topped the Icelandic charts and was a Top Ten hit in four other countries. The album's accolades included the Icelandic Music Award for Album of the Year and the Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album, while Björk won the Icelandic Music Awards for Artist of the Year, Female Singer of the Year, and Composer of the Year, and won her second Brit Award for Best International Female Solo artist. Additionally, Spike Jonze's vivid music video for "It's Oh So Quiet," which took inspiration from vintage Hollywood musicals, was nominated for the Best Music Video Grammy award. To support the album, Björk embarked on her first official tour of North America with [Aphex Twin](spotify:artist:6kBDZFXuLrZgHnvmPu9NsG), and chronicled the European leg of the tour as well as the making of the album in the book Post. November 1996 saw the release of Telegram, a collection of remixes featuring contributions from [LFO](spotify:artist:2M0T4a1pkOC5nifN9W6e9e), Massey, Deodato, [Dillinja](spotify:artist:5CDTMeaU6dnv24n6e4uAtk), and percussionist [Evelyn Glennie](spotify:artist:6MYiQGy8MIcBps6Ez0IQA8). The album reached number 66 on the U.S. charts and peaked at 59 in the U.K. After the lengthy Post tour and an attempt on her life by an obsessed fan, Björk decamped to Málaga, Spain to work on her next album. Seeking a more cohesive approach inspired by Iceland's landscapes, she combined crunchy beats with sweeping strings and worked with co-producers Mark Bell, [Guy Sigsworth](spotify:artist:0uQWT7X0I9Y7zM7WWexpAj), [Howie B](spotify:artist:1DAJPl1Q9bNwPGUqL08nzG), and Markus Dravs, the Icelandic String Octet, and Deodato, who contributed additional string arrangements. Arriving in September 1997, the moody, forceful Homogenic was another triumph: Reaching the Top Ten in 15 countries, it was also certified gold in six countries, including the U.S. Along with earning Björk her third Brit Award for International Female Solo Artist, Homogenic was nominated for the Best Alternative Music Performance Grammy Award, while Gondry's video for the single "Bachelorette" and Chris Cunningham's video for "All Is Full of Love" were nominated for the Best Short Form Music Video Grammy Award in 1999 and 2000, respectively. Early in 1999, Björk started work on Lars von Trier's film Dancer in the Dark, in which she played the main character Selma and wrote and produced the score. At the 2000 Cannes Film Festival, Dancer in the Dark won the Palme d'Or, while Björk was named Best Actress. Later that year, her score for the film appeared as Selmasongs, which included contributions from Homogenic collaborator Bell and "I've Seen It All," a duet with [Radiohead](spotify:artist:4Z8W4fKeB5YxbusRsdQVPb)'s [Thom Yorke](spotify:artist:4CvTDPKA6W06DRfBnZKrau) that earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song. During the challenging Dancer in the Dark shoot, Björk composed quiet, intricate songs that provided a respite as well as a way to celebrate her relationship with artist Matthew Barney. Written and recorded in Spain, Denmark, Iceland, and New York, Vespertine appeared in August 2001 and included contributions from Barney, Jake Davies, [Marius de Vries](spotify:artist:4MEZhJCV2uLCrhZoCzfjVs), Thomas Knak, [Matmos](spotify:artist:0xBkYJzwFzcIYev4fOkvk0), and harpist [Zeena Parkins](spotify:artist:3KI6JsmaN8xyYUq8Tf9Lle). Winning critical acclaim for its delicate sonics and sensual, vulnerable songwriting, the album topped the charts in five countries including Iceland and was certified gold in six countries; in the U.S., it reached number one on the Top Electronic Albums chart. Vespertine was nominated for the Best Alternative Album Grammy Award and the Icelandic Music Award for Album of the Year, while Björk was nominated for the Best International Female Solo Artist Brit Award. She brought [Parkins](spotify:artist:3KI6JsmaN8xyYUq8Tf9Lle), [Matmos](spotify:artist:0xBkYJzwFzcIYev4fOkvk0), and a choir of Inuit women with her on the Vespertine tour, chronicling its smaller-scale performances with the 2002 DVD Live at Royal Opera House and the following year's Miniscule. During this time, she also released Family Tree, a box set gathering rarities and previously unreleased material; Greatest Hits, which collected songs chosen by Björk's fans on her website; and Live Box, a set of live recordings and videos from each of her albums. For her next album, Björk moved away from Vespertine's detailed electronics to focus on the primal power of the human voice. Collaborating with [Robert Wyatt](spotify:artist:5iksmHDN2qZQcgFfXqIXtT), [Mike Patton](spotify:artist:34Ai24gPz5YJ8NbksiNFef), [Rahzel](spotify:artist:6vunRaBya0Sx6CMJZAlHTZ), Japanese beatboxer [Dokaka](spotify:artist:3dsLTMrREVSyX9PRuDibeS), Inuit throat singer [Tanya Tagaq](spotify:artist:2WIb75pwIt78VCAhAtPObY) (who also performed on the Vespertine tour) the Icelandic and London Choirs, [Nico Muhly](spotify:artist:2vObsQCPsbVfkqHlQOu2zc) and [Matmos](spotify:artist:0xBkYJzwFzcIYev4fOkvk0) among many others, she released Medúlla in August 2004. With a title based on the Latin word for "marrow," the largely acapella album earned praise for its experimental approach to the essential qualities of music and vocals. Its global success included placing in the Top Ten of the charts in 19 countries; gold certifications in France and Russia, and silver certification in the U.K.; hitting number one on the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart in the U.S.; and an Icelandic Music Award nomination for Pop Album of the Year. Björk also received Grammy nominations for Best Alternative Album and Best Female Pop Vocal Performance for the track "Oceania," which she performed at the opening ceremony for the 2004 Summer Olympics in Athens, Greece. The following year, she worked with Barney on his film Drawing Restraint 9, acting in it as well as composing its soundtrack. She also appeared in Screaming Masterpiece, a 2005 documentary about Iceland's musical community. Late in 2006, she and the rest of [the Sugarcubes](spotify:artist:1G0Xwj8mza6b03iYkVdzDP) reunited for a performance benefitting the band's former label [Smekkleysa](spotify:search:label%3A%22Smekkleysa%22). In 2007, Björk's cover of [Joni Mitchell](spotify:artist:5hW4L92KnC6dX9t7tYM4Ve)'s "The Boho Dance," which appeared on A Tribute to Joni Mitchell, preceded the May release of her sixth album Volta. A percussive, playful work, its contributors included [Timbaland](spotify:artist:5Y5TRrQiqgUO4S36tzjIRZ), [Toumani Diabaté](spotify:artist:2nCACYdIndYchzX4bxLcTW), Antony Hegarty, [Konono No. 1](spotify:artist:6Sr77iisVrcSg7bQfqqRHk), and an all-female Icelandic brass section. Reaching the Top Ten in 18 countries (including the U.S., making it her highest-placing album there), it was certified silver in the U.K. Like its predecessor, the album was nominated for Grammy and Icelandic Music Awards. Björk toured in support of Volta for a year and a half, with the 2009 set Voltaic, which was released in sets ranging from a CD/DVD to limited multi-disc and vinyl editions, capturing select performances. During the Volta tour, Björk continued to work on music, releasing the single "Náttúra" in October 2008. In 2010, she worked with [Dirty Projectors](spotify:artist:5VF0YkVLeVD4ytyiyVSIiF) on the Mount Wittenberg Orca EP, appeared on albums by [Ólöf Arnalds](spotify:artist:4S3XJRZ2bToEYIH1slOdl5) and [Anohni](spotify:artist:6VJZYivuYJGCrPuOAnI7Qo), and paid tribute to her late collaborator and friend Alexander McQueen by performing at the designer's funeral and contributing the previously unreleased song "Trance" to the short film To Lee, With Love. That year, she also received the Polar Music Prize from the Royal Swedish Academy of Music along with [Ennio Morricone](spotify:artist:1nIUhcKHnK6iyumRyoV68C). Björk's next project, Biophilia, was one of her most ambitious. An interactive exploration of humanity's relationships to sound and the universe that educated its audience about music theory and science, it took shape with the help of engineers, scientists, custom-built instruments, and video game designers. Released as a suite of apps for the iPad and iPhone and on CD, Biophilia arrived in October 2011. A Top Ten hit in six countries, the album once again topped the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart in the U.S. and was nominated for the Best Alternative Album Grammy Award and several Icelandic Music Awards. Bastards, a collection of Biophilia remixes featuring [Death Grips](spotify:artist:5RADpgYLOuS2ZxDq7ggYYH) and [Omar Souleyman](spotify:artist:11dMqVZY4PHgVL80tejvHK), was released in Europe in late 2012 and in the U.S. in early 2013. The Biophilia apps were translated to Android in July 2013, the same month that When Björk Met Attenborough, a BBC Channel 4 documentary with [Sir David Attenborough](spotify:artist:4QJpMVEZA1B0MkdW0jDMX4) and scientist Oliver Sacks that related Biophilia to humanity's relationship with music, premiered. In 2014, Björk contributed vocals to [Death Grips](spotify:artist:5RADpgYLOuS2ZxDq7ggYYH)' album Niggas on the Moon. She also continued the Biophilia project with a live concert film, Biophilia Live. Filmed at London's Alexandra Palace and featuring spectacular visuals, it was released theatrically and in DVD and Blu-ray sets that included the live audio on CD. That year, the Biophilia apps were added to the Museum of Modern Art's permanent collection. By late 2014, Björk was putting the finishing touches on her next album. Featuring collaborations with [Arca](spotify:artist:4SQdUpG4f7UbkJG3cJ2Iyj) and [the Haxan Cloak](spotify:artist:543jOiqi5zLNZIOv7rA6rg), Vulnicura was released in January 2015 after it leaked ahead of its scheduled March release date. Tracing the aftermath of Björk's relationship with Barney and harking back to the string and beat-heavy sounds of Vespertine and Homogenic, the album earned rave reviews for its powerful emotional impact. Topping the Icelandic charts and reaching number 11 in the U.K., Vulnicura also charted throughout Europe and was a Top 20 hit in the U.S. It won Best Album at the Icelandic Music Awards, and Björk won the awards for Best Female Artist, Best Songwriter, and Best Producer. At that year's Brit Awards, she was named International Female Solo Artist (marking her fifth Brit Award), and Vulnicura was nominated for the Best Alternative Music Grammy Award, her seventh nomination in that category. In March 2015, the Museum of Modern Art launched a multimedia exhibit documenting Björk's career from Debut through Vulnicura. It presented her notebooks, costumes, the instruments created for Biophilia, and videos, including a film for the Vulnicura song "Black Lake" by director Andrew Thomas Huang commissioned by the museum. The book Björk: Archives chronicled the exhibition. That March, Björk also embarked on the Vulnicura world tour, backed by [Alarm Will Sound](spotify:artist:3FivPgIIWpeGTnTx5PrpCX) and percussionist [Manu Delago](spotify:artist:08LrhaMKwKuGbB9XHBEjXF), with [Arca](spotify:artist:4SQdUpG4f7UbkJG3cJ2Iyj) joining on theater dates and [the Haxan Cloak](spotify:artist:543jOiqi5zLNZIOv7rA6rg) on festival shows. A series of Vulnicura remixes kicked off in July, with [Lotic](spotify:artist:7o2Y6TQr9B0ynZGhUDAkyj), [Katie Gately](spotify:artist:6FP6ynzSPeBFX46vkI1OsW), [Mica Levi](spotify:artist:29LOCR81IrdEJjCAeCEOU3), [Rabit](spotify:artist:2X3e2rDdxibDfJGv0CwS7A), Juliana Huxtable, and Björk herself among the artists reworking the album's tracks. [One Little Indian](spotify:search:label%3A%22One+Little+Indian%22) gathered all 12 remixes in a limited edition vinyl set that December, the same month that "Stonemilker" was released as a VR app including a 360-degree video and a string-based mix of the song. An acoustic version of Vulnicura, Vulnicura Strings, arrived at the end of 2015 and featured the viola organista, a keyboard-driven string instrument designed by Leonardo da Vinci. Vulnicura Live, which featured Björk's favorite performances of the album's songs as well as some chosen from her other albums, was given a limited release; wider distribution followed in 2016. That June saw the premiere of Björk Digital, a touring exhibit collecting the VR videos created for Vulnicura (one of the videos, "Notget VR," won the Cannes Lions Grand Prix Award for Real Time Virtual Reality Experience). At the exhibit's Tokyo date, Björk performed "Quicksand" during YouTube's first ever virtual reality live stream broadcast. Starting in September, she performed a small acoustic tour with stops including London's Royal Albert Hall and Los Angeles' Walt Disney Concert Hall. In 2017, Björk reunited with [Arca](spotify:artist:4SQdUpG4f7UbkJG3cJ2Iyj) for the follow-up to Vulnicura. The lighter but still complex Utopia, which featured Icelandic and Venezuelan birdsong, an all-female flute section, and lyrics inspired by science fiction and folklore, arrived in November 2017. Charting globally, the album reached number 25 on the U.K. Albums Chart and number 75 on the Billboard 200 in the U.S. Utopia was nominated for Best Alternative Music Album at the 61st Annual Grammy Awards, becoming her eighth consecutive nomination in that category and her 15th nomination overall. The album spawned several singles and EPs: 2017's Blissing Me EP featured a collaboration with [serpentwithfeet](spotify:artist:1O9iHQjrVuiAYOJFCBeFSl); 2018's Arisen My Senses EP included remixes by [Lanark Artefax](spotify:artist:02fDf7HEPtBZLtPzCyxSR2), [Jlin](spotify:artist:23QKqAkKwti9zBiac6RFBA), and [Kelly Lee Owens](spotify:artist:5eitAUlYmlha3LLWg7aBn5); and the following year's Country Creatures EP collected remixes of "Creatures Features" by [Fever Ray](spotify:artist:5hE6NCoobhyEu6TRSbjOJY) and [the Knife](spotify:artist:7eQZTqEMozBcuSubfu52i4) along with Björk's remix of the [Fever Ray](spotify:artist:5hE6NCoobhyEu6TRSbjOJY) song "This Country." Following the initial run of dates in support of the album, in 2019 Björk launched the Cornucopia tour, an ambitious live experience that combined imagery and projections by director Tobias Gremmler and the choir that performed on the album with other musical and visual artists. That year, Björk also shared the stage with [Arca](spotify:artist:4SQdUpG4f7UbkJG3cJ2Iyj), performing "Afterwards," a song that appeared on [Arca](spotify:artist:4SQdUpG4f7UbkJG3cJ2Iyj)'s 2020 album KiCk 1. She then appeared in Robert Eggers' 2022 film The Northman, marking her first film appearance since Drawing Restraint 9. That September saw the release of her tenth album Fossora. Named for a Latin word meaning "digging" and informed by the 2018 death of her mother, the album combined clarinets, flutes, and strings with choral vocals as well as performances by [serpentwithfeet](spotify:artist:1O9iHQjrVuiAYOJFCBeFSl) and [Emilie Nicolas](spotify:artist:4cXE1g28uYrIaUisUx5cJt). The album reached number four on the Icelandic charts and number 11 in the U.K.; in the U.S., it peaked at 100 on the 200 Albums chart and number two on the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart. Another nominee for the Best Alternative Music Album Grammy Award, Fossora took home the Alternative Album of the Year and Recording Direction of the Year prizes at the Icelandic Music Awards. ~ Heather Phares & Stephen Thomas Erlewine, Rovi
